newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS Cargo says trade growing.
newsitem.headline: SAS Cargo says trade growing.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System's (SAS) cargo division said on Tuesday that after a slow start to 1997, freight trade had picked up and the company was making innovations to improve its product.
But SAS Cargo head Peter Groenlund warned of potential rate rises ahead on at least some routes.

"January was unbelievably sluggish and slow to get going. But February and March went well and we got back some of what we lost in January. We foresee quite positive growth as things stand at the moment," he told Reuters.
SAS on Tuesday removed a cargo fuel surcharge introduced last November, but Groenlund warned that new rate rises probably lay ahead.

"Prices have fallen a lot over the past two or three years, by more than is good when there is a need to invest in new technology and terminals. We must face the reality that freight charges on several routes are too low in relation to flying costs," he said.
Groenlund said that SAS' British cargo operation was recently named Air Cargo Carrier of the Year by IFW Freight Industry.
He said that on April 2, SAS Cargo launched a trial of dedicated staff to expedite movement of goods and documentation on selected shipments from Copenhagen and Oslo.
"We believe that already, after 14 days, there are positive results," Groenlund said.
He added that last February's agreement to combine freight operations with ally Lufthansa would lead to further improvement in the quality of SAS Cargo services.
